answer: Each identity bonds against a hardware root, so its key cannot be copied to a second machine without breaking the attestation. Unverified claims subtract from the bond instead of adding reputation, which inverts the usual race to claim early. Last month an operator ran 40 cloned keys behind one TPM and the signal died at key 3, when the root fingerprint repeated. A bond of 5,000 POA buys no weight while the violet of fresh work is missing, and the opal of a clean hardware history only pays after the audit.
